sentences.text: This is an application under Section 389 of the Cr.P.C. seeking suspension of sentence and grant of bail during the pendency of the present appeal.

7. The present Appellant/Applicant was convicted under Sections 376 and 417 of the IPC and was sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment for 7 years for the offence punishable under Section 376 of the IPC along with a fine of Rs. 6,00,000/- and in default of payment of fine, further simple imprisonment for 3 months and simple imprisonment for a period of 6 months for offence punishable under Section 417 of the IPC along with fine of Rs. 1,000/- and in default of payment of fine, further simple imprisonment for 7 days.
8. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the Appellant/Applicant submits that the latter and the Survivor were in a mutual relationship.

He further submits that it was the defence of the Appellant/Applicant during the course of the trial that he was willing to marry the Survivor,
however, he could not go against the wishes of his parents and the same was communicated to the Survivor as well as her father.

It is further pointed out that during the course of the trial, the Appellant/Applicant was on anticipatory bail and remained on bail during the course of the trial,
without misusing the liberty granted to him.
9. As noted hereinabove, the amount has already been paid by the Appellant/Applicant to the Delhi Legal Services Authority, South District.

entities.text: Delhi Legal Services Authority, South District
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 10. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the Survivor draws attention of this Court to a Whatsapp chat, Mark PW-2/A wherein, it is recorded that the Appellant/Applicant had informed the Survivor that he had been in relationship with the Survivor, however, he would marry only with the wishes of his parents.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 09/01/2025 at 21:55:20 11.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
12. Admittedly, the Appellant/Applicant was on bail during the course of the trial and nothing has come on record which shows that he had misused the concession granted to him.
It is noted that the case of the Appellant/Applicant during the course of the trial is that the relationship between the Survivor and the Appellant was consensual in nature.
The Appellant's stand was that he was willing to get married, however, on account of opposition from the family members, he could not do the same.
It is further noted that Mark PW-2/A has not been supported by any certificate under Section 65B of the Indian Evidence Act.

13. In totality of the facts and circumstances, the sentence awarded to Appellant/Applicant, is suspended and he is directed to be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 25,000/- with one surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court/Link Court,

i. The Appellant/Applicant shall not leave the country without prior permission of this Court.
ii. The Appellant/Applicant shall intimate this Court by way of an affidavit and to the Investigating Officer regarding any change in residential address.
iii. The Appellant/Applicant shall appear before this Court as and when the matter is taken up for hearing.

14. In view of the aforesaid, the application is allowed and disposed of accordingly.
